transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I came in because I’ve been having these times where, after a really long day on site or after a neighborhood meeting, I get home and just eat way more than I meant to. Like leftover takeout, cereal, chips—whatever’s around. I keep going until I’m really uncomfortably full, and it’s been bothering me.

Can you tell me more about those times when you eat more than you meant to? Do you feel like you can’t stop yourself or control how much you eat, and do you ever make yourself sick or do anything else to try to balance it out afterward?

Yeah… once I start on those evenings, it kind of feels like I’m on autopilot. I’ll be telling myself, “Stop, you’ve got an early crew start,” but then I still go back to the kitchen for more. It doesn’t feel like I’m really choosing it at that point.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or doing extra exercise?

Yeah… a few times a month, after those nights, I do make myself throw up. I go into the bathroom and do it because I start panicking that I’ve ruined all the work I’ve put into looking put-together. I don’t really use laxatives, and it’s not usually exercise—it’s mostly that.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports loss of control during eating episodes and compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting). This aligns with the diagnostic criteria for bulimia nervosa (F50.2). Other candidates (F50.0, F50.8, F50.9) are ruled out based on the presence of compensatory behaviors and pattern of disordered eating.
